column1: # go-test-weights.tsv - per-package `go test -race` wall-clock, in seconds.
# Lines starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored by the reader.
# Consumed by scripts/ci/go-test-shards.sh to balance the CI shards. These
# weights are a HEURISTIC ONLY: a package missing here is simply assumed cheap,
# and a stale number costs balance, never correctness - the package universe is
# recomputed from `go list` on every run and `go-test-shards.sh check` fails the
# job if any package would go unrun.
# Source (lane TESTCI, item 7 of the test-time plan, 2026-10-29): the
# previous table summed to 28.1 h against a measured full run of 4.37 h
# (internal/mcp weighted 2351 s, measured 21 s). Regenerated from:
# - 623 packages: the max of two ci runs, via
#   run 39364803173 (a full run, -race on every package) and run 39014355005
#   (a push, -race on the concurrent list only; for a package off that list
#   this is its plain time, which the max keeps only when it is larger).
#   Both measured with checkptr off for modernc.org.
# - 139 packages new since those runs (sandbox, security and org security
#   packages among them): measured on the lane host (4 cores) under -race
#   with checkptr off for modernc.org, times 1.8 for the 2-vCPU runner (the
#   same rule the D-604 table used for packages a ci run never finished).
#   internal/orgserver/secorg was the heaviest package of the suite (1808 s
#   locally, 3254 s here: serial tests that each migrated an org database
#   from zero). Lane testfu (2026-10-29) moved its fixtures onto the shared
#   migrated template and re-measured on a 4-core lane host under -race with
#   checkptr off for modernc.org: 2025 s before, 13.5 s after with a warm
#   template and 44 s with a cold one (the template build included); the row
#   internal/testsupport/latencygate): 1 s each, measured under 0.1 s.
# Every test package of the tree (764) has a row; no hand overrides remain.
